page: UpCloud DEV-2xCPU-4GB is a developer-class virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 60 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng CPU tests and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, because the CPU resources are shared, multi-core benchmarks show limitations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores fall into the weak category, while Passmark memory performance is rated as poor. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations remains average.

This server is designed for budget-conscious development environments where continuous, intensive multi-core execution is not required. The shared CPU allocation provides a cost-efficient entry point for lightweight tasks, though it introduces resource contention risks under sustained loads. It is best suited for software development, testing, single-threaded scripting, lightweight static web serving, and basic text or prompt processing using small models.
